question: According to Universal Adult Franchise in India, what is the minimum age required to vote in elections? 🗳️
explanation: Awesome! In India, any citizen who is 18 years or older has the equal right to cast their vote and choose their leaders! 🗳️
hint: It is the age when a person legally becomes an adult in India.

question: What does the word 'Franchise' mean in the context of elections? 📜
explanation: Fantastic! In political science, franchise or suffrage simply means the beautiful right given to citizens to vote! 📜
hint: It is the power citizens use to elect their representatives.

question: What does 'Universal' mean in Universal Adult Franchise? 🌍
options: Everyone has the right to vote equally 🤝
answer: Everyone has the right to vote equally 🤝
explanation: Great job! It means every adult citizen, regardless of their wealth, caste, religion, or gender, has an equal right to vote! 🌍
hint: It implies equality for all adult citizens.

question: Which independent body is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India? 🇮🇳
explanation: Brilliant! The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a super important independent body that organizes and manages all major elections! 🇮🇳
hint: Look for the option with 'Commission' in its name.

question: What is the full form of EVM used during voting? 💻
explanation: Excellent! An EVM is an Electronic Voting Machine, which helps us cast our votes easily by pressing a button! 💻
hint: It uses electronics to record your choice.

question: What does 'Secret Ballot' mean in a democracy? 🤫
options: Keeping your vote private and safe 🤫
Whispering your vote to the officer 🗣️
answer: Keeping your vote private and safe 🤫
explanation: Perfect! Secret ballot means nobody else will know who you voted for, ensuring you can choose freely without any pressure! 🤫
hint: It is about keeping your choice completely private.

question: What is the special button called NOTA on an EVM? 🛑
explanation: Spot on! NOTA stands for 'None Of The Above', giving voters a choice if they feel no candidate is suitable! 🛑
hint: It means you do not choose any of the listed options.

question: What happens when a voter presses the button next to a candidate's name on the EVM? 🔴
options: A red light glows and a beep sound is heard 🔴
answer: A red light glows and a beep sound is heard 🔴
explanation: Awesome! When you press the button, a red light glows and a loud beep confirms your vote has been successfully recorded! 🔴
hint: It involves a light and a sound to confirm your action.

question: Which document is officially known as EPIC and is used to cast a vote? 🪪
explanation: Great job! EPIC stands for Electors Photo Identity Card, which is commonly known as the Voter ID card! 🪪
hint: It has your photo and is specifically made for elections.

question: Why is indelible ink applied to a voter's finger? ☝️
options: To make the finger look pretty 💅
To show they support a party 🚩
To ensure they vote only once ☝️
answer: To ensure they vote only once ☝️
explanation: Fantastic! The special ink stays on the finger for a few days, ensuring the voting process is fair and nobody votes twice! ☝️
hint: It prevents double voting.

question: What do we call the official list of all the people who are eligible to vote in an area? 📜
explanation: Brilliant! The Electoral Roll is the super important official list containing the names of everyone who can vote! 📜
hint: It has 'Voter' in its everyday name.

question: What is the specific geographical area called from where voters elect one representative? 🗺️
explanation: Excellent! For elections, the country is divided into smaller areas called constituencies, and each elects one leader! 🗺️
hint: It starts with the letter 'C'.

question: What is the main purpose of an Election Symbol given to a political party? 🌸
options: To help voters easily identify the party 🌸
answer: To help voters easily identify the party 🌸
explanation: Perfect! Symbols help everyone, especially those who cannot read, to quickly and easily recognize their favorite party! 🌸
hint: It makes identification quick and simple.

question: Who allocates these unique election symbols to political parties in India? 🎖️
explanation: Awesome! The Election Commission is the helpful body that assigns fair and unique symbols to all parties! 🎖️
hint: It is the same body that conducts the elections.

question: In a democracy, the principle of 'One Person, One Vote' ensures what? ⚖️
options: Only one person rules the country 👑
explanation: Great job! 'One Person, One Vote, One Value' ensures beautiful political equality, meaning every citizen's voice is equally important! ⚖️
hint: It is about fairness and equal treatment.

question: What is the full form of VVPAT, a machine attached to the EVM? 🖨️
explanation: Fantastic! VVPAT is a wonderful machine that prints a small paper slip so you can verify your vote was cast correctly! 🖨️
hint: It involves a paper audit trail.

question: How long is the VVPAT paper slip visible to the voter behind the glass window? ⏳
explanation: Brilliant! The printed slip is safely visible for about 7 seconds, letting you smile knowing your vote went to the right candidate! ⏳
hint: It is a very short time, less than 10 seconds.

question: What do political parties release to share their future plans and promises with voters? 📖
explanation: Excellent! A manifesto is a wonderful document where parties share all their positive plans and promises for the future! 📖
hint: It starts with the letter 'M'.

question: What do we call a person who stands in an election to be chosen as a leader? 🙋
explanation: Perfect! A candidate is an enthusiastic person who contests the election, hoping to serve the people! 🙋
hint: It starts with the letter 'C'.

question: Which of these is a major advantage of using Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)? 🌳
options: They save millions of trees by reducing paper use 🌳
answer: They save millions of trees by reducing paper use 🌳
explanation: Awesome! EVMs are incredibly eco-friendly because they eliminate the need for printing millions of paper ballots! 🌳
hint: Think about nature and saving paper.

question: When do all election campaigning and public meetings officially stop? ⏰
options: On the morning of the election 🌅
explanation: Great job! Campaigning peacefully stops 48 hours before polling ends so voters can think quietly and make their choice! ⏰
hint: It is exactly two days before.

question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India? 🇮🇳
explanation: Fantastic! The President of India proudly appoints the Chief Election Commissioner to ensure fair elections! 🇮🇳
hint: It is the highest constitutional post in the country.

question: What is the set of rules issued by the Election Commission to guide the conduct of political parties and candidates? 📜
explanation: Brilliant! The Model Code of Conduct ensures that all parties play fair and respect the election rules wonderfully! 📜
hint: It is a 'Model' way of behaving.

question: In a democracy, who holds the ultimate power? 🤝
explanation: Excellent! Democracy is a government of the people, so the real and ultimate power always belongs to the wonderful citizens! 🤝
hint: It is you, your parents, and all the common citizens.

question: What happens if a candidate is not a member of any political party? 🚶
options: They contest as an Independent candidate 🚶
answer: They contest as an Independent candidate 🚶
explanation: Perfect! Anyone meeting the rules can courageously contest elections on their own as an Independent candidate! 🚶
hint: They stand 'independently'.

question: What do we call the place where citizens go to cast their votes? 🏫
explanation: Awesome! A polling booth or polling station is a safely arranged place, usually a school, where people go to vote! 🏫
hint: It is a temporary setup in schools or public buildings.

question: Which finger is marked with indelible ink during voting? ☝️
explanation: Great job! The friendly polling officer puts a small mark on your left index finger to show you have successfully voted! ☝️
hint: It is the pointing finger on your left hand.

question: When did women in India get the right to vote? 🇮🇳
options: From the very first general election 🇮🇳
answer: From the very first general election 🇮🇳
explanation: Fantastic! India is amazing because it gave the equal right to vote to both men and women right from the very first election! 🇮🇳
hint: They got it immediately along with everyone else.

question: Usually, how often are general elections for the Lok Sabha held in India? ⏳
explanation: Brilliant! We happily celebrate the festival of democracy by electing a new Lok Sabha government every 5 years! ⏳
hint: Count the fingers on one hand.

question: What is it called when an election is held again in a single constituency because a seat becomes vacant? 🗳️
explanation: Excellent! A by-election is a special voting event held quickly to fill a single seat so the people remain represented! 🗳️
hint: It has the prefix 'By'.

question: Which of these is NOT a role of the Election Commission? ❌
explanation: Perfect! The Election Commission focuses solely on organizing great elections, while other government departments build roads! 🌉
hint: Look for the task related to construction, not elections.

question: EVMs are useful because they can run without what? 🔌
explanation: Awesome! EVMs cleverly run on secure batteries, which means voting can happen even in remote areas without power! 🔌
hint: They use batteries instead.

question: What do we call the party that gets the maximum number of seats and forms the government? 🏛️
explanation: Great job! The Ruling Party is the victorious team that forms the government to wonderfully serve the country! 🏛️
hint: They are the ones 'ruling' or managing the government.

question: What is the role of the Opposition Party in a democracy? 🗣️
options: To question the government and ensure they work well 🗣️
answer: To question the government and ensure they work well 🗣️
explanation: Fantastic! The Opposition plays a brilliant role by asking important questions and helping the government make better decisions! 🗣️
hint: They keep a check on the ruling party.

question: If no single party gets a majority, they might join with other parties to form what kind of government? 🤝
explanation: Brilliant! When parties team up together beautifully, they form a 'Coalition Government' to run the country! 🤝
hint: It starts with a 'C' and means coming together.

question: Before casting a vote, the polling officer checks your identity against which list? 📜
explanation: Excellent! The friendly polling officer safely checks the Electoral Roll to confirm your name is registered to vote! 📜
hint: It is the official voter list.

question: What is the minimum age to contest (stand as a candidate) in Lok Sabha elections? 🧑‍💼
explanation: Perfect! While you can vote at 18, you must be a responsible 25 years old to stand as a candidate for the Lok Sabha! 🧑‍💼
hint: It is 7 years more than the voting age.

question: Who helps the Election Commission conduct elections at the polling booths? 👮
explanation: Awesome! Many dedicated government employees, like school teachers, proudly work as polling officers to help us vote safely! 👮
hint: They are everyday public servants.

question: What makes counting votes with an EVM better than paper ballots? ⏱️
options: It is extremely fast and accurate ⏱️
answer: It is extremely fast and accurate ⏱️
explanation: Great job! EVMs are modern marvels that make counting incredibly fast and completely error-free! ⏱️
hint: Think about speed and correctness.

question: Which core value of the Indian Constitution is upheld by the Universal Adult Franchise? ⚖️
explanation: Fantastic! It beautifully upholds Equality, showing that every single citizen is equally precious to the nation! ⚖️
hint: It means treating everyone exactly the same.

question: What should you do before the election day to ensure you can vote? ✔️
options: Check if your name is on the Electoral Roll ✔️
answer: Check if your name is on the Electoral Roll ✔️
explanation: Brilliant! Being a smart citizen means you always check that your name is happily listed on the voter list beforehand! ✔️
hint: Verify your registration status.

question: During an election campaign, candidates travel to meet voters and hold what? 🎤
explanation: Excellent! Candidates hold exciting public rallies to share their great ideas and listen to the people's needs! 🎤
hint: These are large gatherings of people to listen to speeches.

question: The right to vote is given to us by which supreme law book of the country? 📖
explanation: Perfect! Our glorious Constitution of India grants us all the powerful and equal right to vote! 📖
hint: It is the supreme law book of our country.

question: How are EVMs safely kept after voting is finished? 🔒
options: Sealed and kept in a highly secure 'Strong Room' 🔒
answer: Sealed and kept in a highly secure 'Strong Room' 🔒
explanation: Awesome! EVMs are securely sealed and protected by armed guards in a safe place called a Strong Room until counting day! 🔒
hint: It is a room known for its strength and security.

question: Why does the Election Commission set up ramps at polling booths? ♿
options: To make it easy for elderly and differently-abled voters to enter ♿
answer: To make it easy for elderly and differently-abled voters to enter ♿
explanation: Great job! The ECI is very caring and sets up ramps so that elderly and differently-abled citizens can vote comfortably! ♿
hint: It helps people using wheelchairs.

question: What does a free and fair election mean? 🕊️
options: Voting is free of cost but unfair ❌
Voters can vote without any fear, bribe, or pressure 🕊️
Only a few people can vote 🙋
Candidates can force people to vote 😠
answer: Voters can vote without any fear, bribe, or pressure 🕊️
explanation: Fantastic! Free and fair elections mean every citizen feels completely safe and joyful while casting their honest vote! 🕊️
hint: It means no one forces or scares you into voting for them.

question: Which of these systems did India use before the invention of the EVM? 🗳️
explanation: Brilliant! Long ago, people used paper ballots and safely dropped them into large metal boxes to cast their votes! 🗳️
hint: It involved pieces of paper and a box.

question: In a multi-party system like India, how many political parties can exist? 🇮🇳
explanation: Excellent! India has a vibrant multi-party system, meaning many wonderful parties can exist and compete fairly! 🇮🇳
hint: The word 'multi' means more than one or two.

question: How does casting a vote help a citizen? 🌟
options: It gives them a voice in how their country is run 🌟
It gives them a free trip ✈️
It gives them an EVM to keep 💻
answer: It gives them a voice in how their country is run 🌟
explanation: Perfect! Every single vote is a powerful voice that helps build a brighter and happier future for the nation! 🌟
hint: It empowers them to participate in nation-building.

question: What is the phrase often used in India to describe the joyous process of elections? 🎉
explanation: Awesome! Elections are proudly celebrated as the 'Festival of Democracy' because it is a time when the power of the people shines brightest! 🎉
hint: It sounds like a grand celebration.
